summary: Arduino Uno R3 controls a two-wheel differential-drive robot through an L298N motor driver. An HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor measures obstacle distance and an MG995 servo positions the sensor. A computer running the Python agent and navigation pipeline communicates over USB serial. The design uses non-blocking control timing and a fail-safe motor stop.

components.role: Two DC motor direction and speed control
Multi-agent pipeline, path planning and serial communication

pin_map.note: MG995 servo control using Servo library

power.motor_supply: External motor supply matched to the actual DC motor voltage and current ratings, connected through the L298N.
power.servo_supply: Separate regulated 5-6 V supply with adequate current capacity for the MG995.
power.notes: Do not power the MG995 directly from an Arduino GPIO or rely on the Uno 5 V pin to supply its motor current.

states.name: STOPPED
states.entry: Both motor enable signals are set to zero.

states.name: FORWARD
states.entry: Both motors move forward at the configured speed.

states.name: TURNING
states.entry: Differential motor control performs a timed turn.

states.name: OBSTACLE
states.entry: Both motors stop while obstacle data is processed.

transitions.when: A valid forward command is received and the path is clear.
A valid obstacle measurement is below the safety threshold.
The navigation controller issues a valid turn command.
A stop command, sensor fault or communication timeout occurs.

modules.name: motors
modules.responsibility: L298N direction and PWM speed control.

modules.name: ultrasonic
modules.responsibility: HC-SR04 trigger, echo timing and distance calculation.

modules.name: servo
modules.responsibility: MG995 positioning for directional sensor scans.

modules.name: control
modules.responsibility: Safe motor control and robot state transitions.

safety: motorsStop() is called during setup before any motor movement. Both motors stop when an obstacle is detected within the configured threshold. Invalid ultrasonic readings and echo timeouts are treated as unsafe measurements. Invalid commands and serial communication timeouts must result in a motor stop. The MG995 uses a separate regulated supply and all relevant grounds are common.
